newsitem.title: UK: W. Africa Suezmaxes dip, other tanker sectors stab.
newsitem.headline: W. Africa Suezmaxes dip, other tanker sectors stab.

text.p: West Africa/U.S. 130,000 tonne dirty tanker rates softened on Monday on an increase in tonnage now that most March stems have been fixed, brokers said.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf 130,000 tonne (Suezmax) rates edged down to W102.5/W105 from W107.5 after firming steadily last week.
"March stems are now out of the way and looking at April, there are a reasonable number of ships available. We could go below W100 by the end of the week," one broker said.

West Africa very large crude carriers (VLCCs) were stable at around W72.5, as were VLCCs from the Middle East Gulf, except to Singapore which edged down to W62.5. Mideast/west VLCCs remained at W57.5 and Mideast/Japan at W67.5

Some brokers said the Mediterranean had softened slightly with the West African market, but an Italian broker said there had been good enquiry on 70,000 tonners with at least six cargoes seeking homes. "Not bad for a Monday -- we will see if rates go up tomorrow," he added.
The North Sea/transatlantic market was flat, with the 275,000 tonne Chios fetching W77.5 for a Mongstad/EC Canada voyage for Irving, loading April 6.
The inter-U.K./Cont market maintained its recent firm tone, with 80,000 tonners continuing to be fixed at about W140.
Fuel oil was also steady, with 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont at W195 and cross-Med at W220.
There was similarly little change in the Caribs/upcoast sector, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W205 and 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil at about W202.5, brokers said.
